title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government has outlined its stance on the Committee’s 2020 report, clarifying how it will support the development and adoption of public standards for AI. It commits to collaboration, transparency, and oversight to ensure AI technologies are safe, ethical, and aligned with societal values.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual has outlined how it will regulate the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector, setting rules and guidance for exam boards, training providers and other stakeholders. The policy was released after a joint request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: This report examines how artificial intelligence systems utilize copyrighted materials, analyzing the legal, economic, and societal impacts of such use. It offers recommendations for stakeholders to balance the protection of creators' rights with the need for AI development and innovation.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The UK government responded to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence’s report “AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency” by outlining measures to improve regulation, safety, and ethical use of AI technologies. It commits to strengthening oversight, investing in research, protecting workers, and ensuring AI benefits society while mitigating risks.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: The document explains the purpose, scope, and responsibilities of a committee that will review how artificial intelligence affects public standards. It also provides answers to common questions about the committee’s process and objectives.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has provided written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee’s inquiry on the Governance of Artificial Intelligence, offering its viewpoint on how AI should be regulated and monitored. The submission likely discusses key governance issues such as transparency, accountability, and policy recommendations to guide future AI regulation.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: This policy explores how artificial intelligence will affect the rules governing medical products, aiming to update safety and approval processes. It applies the guidelines from the AI White Paper to ensure transparent, reliable, and secure use of AI in medical device regulation.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy aims to make the defense organization the most effective, efficient, trusted, and influential AI leader for its size. It focuses on developing and deploying AI responsibly to enhance national security capabilities.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport Artificial Intelligence Action Plan shows how the Department for Transport will partner with the transport sector to use AI for safer, more efficient and sustainable travel. It also sets out ways to spot and manage the risks of AI, such as data privacy, security, bias and regulatory concerns.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: The report updates on how copyrighted works are being used to train AI systems, assessing current practices and legal compliance under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act. It highlights progress made, identifies challenges and gaps, and offers recommendations to improve the balance between protecting copyright and fostering AI innovation.
